name: Dietitian

pf.license.need: always for medical nutrition therapy: a dietitian's own license where the state's form licenses dietitians, or the national dietitian registration (RDN) as the proof where the state's form has no license (a switch)
pf.license.who: each person; the practice too, only where the state's form registers nutrition practices (a switch)
pf.license.ask: each dietitian's license number and state, and their registration number, in the invite reply (or the owner sends them); a diabetes educator's certificate number for diabetes education
pf.license.check: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.remote: a video visit only with a dietitian licensed for the state the client is in during that visit, or registered where that state's form has no license, or holding a permit the state's form allows (a switch); the state is asked before times and confirmed at the start of each video visit
pf.license.coach: a nutrition coach with no dietitian license is booked only for general wellness coaching and grocery store tours, never for medical nutrition therapy, a health condition, a doctor's referral, a plan or anyone under 18; where the state's form limits all one-on-one nutrition advice to licensed dietitians, coaching stays off there (a switch)
pf.license.diabetesEducation: diabetes education as its own kind of work needs a certified diabetes educator on the team where the plug-in or a plan asks for one (a switch); it waits for that person's certificate
pf.license.agreement: a health privacy agreement (a HIPAA business associate agreement) signed on the secure page before the first booking
pf.license.renewals: optional reminders the owner sets; a license the owner says has lapsed pauses that person's new bookings for that work (the owner's word, never a check)
pf.license.insurance: malpractice insurance where the state's form or a plan asks for it

pf.services.shape: one client with one dietitian at a time, each visit a set length: a 60-minute first nutrition visit (the assessment), then 30-minute follow-ups agreed at the visit and OK'd by the client by text; a new client may ask for a free 15-minute intro call first; a parent or guardian comes with anyone under 18
pf.services.examples: the example practices' own prices (Lee Nutrition Clinic at the clinic and by video, Lee Home Nutrition at clients' homes and stores), not a standard; with a health plan, the client pays the plan's share and the practice bills the plan

pf.services.notOffered: medicine or weight-loss shots (no prescribers); eating-disorder care booked by an AI (the clinic's own team books it by phone, with the client's doctor); lab tests (the client's doctor orders them)
pf.services.capacity: one client, or one family, per dietitian at a time; the clinic's one larger room for a family visit
pf.services.nobodyHome: never: the client is always there
pf.services.online: video visits count as at the clinic: first visits and follow-ups, only with a dietitian licensed for where the client is that day

afterTime: anything that helps at the visit, like an interpreter or a step-free door

the referring doctor's name and practice

whether texts and voicemail are safe, and what a message may say

pf.questions.whoMayBook: an adult for themselves; a parent or guardian for anyone under 18, who comes to the visit (the owner OKs it first); a guardian or health care agent for an adult who can't consent; someone else may pay, but the client agrees for themselves
pf.questions.neverAsked: the condition, weight, lab results, medicine names, eating habits and a child's details are never asked in the AI chat or by text: only on the secure page

stop.words: a medical emergency: fainting, confusion, chest pain, trouble breathing, or very high or very low blood sugar the person can't bring back
stop.say: This sounds like an emergency. Call 911 now. Don't wait for an appointment.

stop.booking: no booking in that chat; if the person is already a client, the owner and their dietitian are told at once with a link, never the words

stop.words: signs of an eating disorder: making yourself throw up, using laxatives to get rid of food, going days without eating, or a strong fear of gaining weight
stop.say: The clinic's own team books this kind of care by phone, together with your doctor. Please also talk with your doctor soon. If you feel faint or unwell now, call 911. If you have thoughts of hurting yourself, call or text 988.
stop.booking: no booking by the AI: the clinic's own line, and no weight-loss or meal-plan visit is offered; the owner is told with a link, never the words

goOn.words: feeling unwell, or a sugar reading that worries them, with nothing above
goOn.what: Rosie says to call their doctor today, and 911 if it gets worse; then booking goes on

goOn.words: a question about food, weight or medicine
goOn.what: no advice from Rosie or the AI: the dietitian answers at the visit, or on the secure page; nothing is quoted in a text

pf.safety.always: the general screen on every message, call and intake answer: danger to life or a medical emergency gets 911, self-harm gets 988; Rosie never gives diet, weight or medical advice, only booking
pf.safety.forms: an intake answer that shows signs of an eating disorder or self-harm reaches the dietitian and the owner the same day, never waiting for the visit

steps.name: Doctor's referral
steps.when: where the client's plan pays for nutrition therapy only with a doctor's referral (often only for some conditions), or where the state's form requires one (a switch); due 2 business days before the visit, so the client hears before free cancel ends
steps.who: clients whose plan or state asks for it
steps.result: the desk logs it when the doctor's practice sends it; not in by the due time: the desk calls the doctor's practice; still missing: the client hears the plan may not pay, and keeps it at self-pay, moves it, or cancels free

steps.name: Intake on the secure page
steps.when: on the secure page only, never by text; due the day before; one reminder
steps.who: every client, and each adult in a family visit
steps.result: not done: the owner keeps the visit (filled in before it starts), moves it, or cancels with no fee

steps.name: The plan check
steps.when: while booking, by the desk, by hand or an electronic check
steps.who: every client who names a plan
steps.result: covered (the share shows), covered only for some conditions or with a referral, not covered (self-pay, or a free cancel), or can't check now (the desk checks by the next business day)

steps.name: Intro call
steps.when: before the first visit, at least a day before; booked with it on one secure link
steps.who: a new client who asks for one
steps.result: a fit: the first visit stands; another dietitian fits better: the client OKs the change; not a fit: cancelled with nothing charged

steps.name: A written good-faith estimate
steps.when: told while booking; sent on time, as the federal rules say
steps.result: a to-do for the desk, with its due date; Rosie delivers it and records when

steps.name: Recent lab results
steps.when: on the secure page, if the client has them
steps.result: never a reason to hold up a visit

pf.first_steps.prep: for a first visit: the medicines and supplements on the secure page, and recent lab results if there are any; for video: a quiet, private place; for a home visit: the kitchen as it usually is; for a grocery store tour: meet at the store's entrance

pf.visit.checkIn: at the clinic: the code at the front desk; by video: read out at the start; at home: the code at the door; a grocery store tour: the code at the store's entrance
pf.visit.beforeWork: the dietitian reads the intake; at a video visit, the dietitian confirms the client's name and where they are, for the license and in case of an emergency
pf.visit.changes: nothing is added during a visit; a longer visit is booked ahead; the dietitian sets the goals with the client at the visit (never Rosie), and the follow-ups agreed there are confirmed by the client's own yes by text
pf.visit.done: the code or DONE; visit notes, goals and any meal plan stay in the practice's own record and on the secure page, never in a text; Rosie keeps only booking notes
pf.visit.missed: a missed visit: no fee unless a card was saved and the owner says yes
pf.visit.home: at home, the dietitian looks in the kitchen and pantry only with the client's OK, and leaves at once if they feel unsafe (they text UNSAFE)

pf.money.before: nothing taken at booking (the example practice keeps no card); where the owner turns on the clinic's $40 late-cancel fee, a card is saved for it, nothing taken, never for a fee-free client
pf.money.plans: the plans the practice takes (its own list); the desk checks each plan by hand or electronically and records it: active or not, in network, whether it covers nutrition therapy for this client's condition, whether it needs a doctor's referral, the share, and the covered hours or visits used and left; the share is an estimate, not a promise
pf.money.referral: where a plan pays only with a doctor's referral, the desk logs it before the visit; without it, the client hears the plan may not pay before the visit, never after
pf.money.selfPay: a self-pay or uninsured client hears while booking that they can get a written good-faith estimate, and gets it on time; a bill far above it can be disputed (the federal rules set how)
pf.money.outOfNetwork: the client pays the self-pay price, and the receipt on the secure page has what their plan needs to pay them back
pf.money.after: at the clinic: the share or the self-pay price at the front desk, and the clinic bills the plan its own way; a self-pay video visit: the bill Rosie texts at DONE; at home and at a store: the bill Rosie texts at DONE, or the business bills the plan its own way; a balance after the plan pays is billed by the practice, never by Rosie's text
pf.money.fees: the late-cancel or missed-visit fee: $40 at the example clinic (the old flowchart's own number), with less than 24 hours' notice; only where the owner turns it on and a card was saved; the same fee for every client who may be charged one; only when the owner confirms; never billed to a plan; no fee for home visits in the example
pf.money.feeFree: a switch from the state's and the plan's rules: no fee ever for clients a plan or the rules protect (like Medicaid, where that applies); for some plans, like Medicare, only if every client pays the same fee; the owner can mark any client fee-free; their texts say 'No fee to cancel or miss'
pf.money.rosfield: the $2 per booking applies to this work, as to every kind of work (D97): a flat fee for each booking Rosie's AI makes, shown at sign-up for the owner's yes; a booking the business puts in itself carries no $2; card payments cost only Stripe's own card fee, paid to Stripe
pf.money.caps: fee limits for plan clients: from the plan's and the state's rules (switches)
pf.money.packages: a package of 3 follow-ups for self-pay clients, sold only at the clinic after the first visit; a follow-up booked from it uses one
pf.money.repeatPlans: follow-ups are dated visits the client says yes to; each is paid when it happens; nothing paid ahead

pf.messages.never: client texts carry only the business name, the date, the time, the place and a secure link: never the kind of visit, a condition, a weight, lab results, a medicine name, food or eating details, or a child's details; at home and at a store, the dietitian's name and photo stay, for the door check; the video link stays on the secure page
pf.messages.staff: texts to the owner and staff use the client's initials (A.M.), the time and a link: never health details, weights, lab results, medicine names or a child's details; a client's question or worrying words go behind a link, never quoted
pf.messages.safeContact: the client says if texts and voicemail are safe; if not, Rosie reaches them only the way they pick
pf.messages.minors: texts about a child's or teen's visit go to the parent or guardian
pf.messages.ratings: a private 1-to-5 rating only the practice sees; no public review request unless the client said yes to marketing texts
pf.messages.noAdvice: Rosie gives no diet, weight or medical advice by text or chat; it answers only about booking

pf.staff.licenses: each dietitian's own license per state, or their registration where a state's form has no license; a diabetes educator's certificate for diabetes education
pf.staff.skills: who sees adults, teens and families; who offers video, home visits and grocery store tours; who speaks which language; who is trained for eating-disorder care (booked only by the clinic's team, by phone); a dietitian with a provisional license works under a supervisor
pf.staff.coach: a nutrition coach (the example practices have none) is offered only for general wellness coaching and grocery store tours, never for medical nutrition therapy, a condition, a referral, a plan or anyone under 18 (a switch from the state's form)
pf.staff.oks: the owner OKs visits for anyone under 18, same-day visits, any custom price, and anything a dietitian flags
pf.staff.standIn: a client's dietitian is never changed without the client's own yes; a stand-in is offered only with the same license for the client's state and the same skills
pf.staff.homeVisits: only dietitians cleared for home visits go to homes
pf.staff.supervision: a dietitian with a provisional license works only under the supervisor the state's form sets (a switch)

pf.rules.records: nutrition records are kept by the practice as long as the state's rules require (a child's may be longer); Rosie keeps only booking and payment records, and a delete removes only those
pf.rules.copies: a client's copy of their records within the time the rules set; Rosie sends only booking and payment records
pf.rules.scope: medical nutrition therapy only by a dietitian the state's form allows: licensed there, or registered where the state has no license (a switch); general wellness coaching by others only where the state's form allows it
pf.rules.referral: where the state's form requires a doctor's referral for medical nutrition therapy (a switch); a plan's own referral rule is checked by the desk
pf.rules.telehealth: video visits follow the state the client is in during the visit (a switch for each state's license rule)
pf.rules.minors: who may consent for a child or teen (switches from the state's form)
pf.rules.goodFaith: the written good-faith estimate for self-pay and uninsured clients, on the federal timeline (a to-do with its due date)
pf.rules.coveredHours: a plan's covered hours or visits for nutrition therapy, counted by the desk; more only as the plan allows, like after a new doctor's order
pf.rules.showLicense: the license shown where the state asks: posted at the clinic, and on the listing
pf.rules.ads: no claims the state's rules don't allow, like promised weight loss
pf.rules.privacy: health privacy rules for every message and form; the business associate agreement before going live

pf.edges.emergency: medical emergency words in any message get 911 at once; self-harm words get 988; the booking stays, and the client's dietitian and the owner are told with a link
pf.edges.eatingDisorder: signs of an eating disorder in any message or intake answer: no automatic booking or change; the clinic's own line, a doctor soon, 911 or 988 as needed; the dietitian and owner are told the same day with a link
pf.edges.foodQuestion: a question about food, weight or medicine: no advice; the dietitian sees it behind a link and answers on the secure page or at the visit
pf.edges.lateArrival: a late client is seen in the time left, and the visit ends on time; no fee for running late
pf.edges.missedVisit: no fee unless a card was saved and the owner confirms
pf.edges.standIn: a dietitian out: new times with the same dietitian, or another only with the client's yes
pf.edges.referral: the referral isn't in: the desk calls the doctor's practice; still missing: self-pay, a move, or a free cancel, before the visit
pf.edges.planChange: the plan check comes back not covered: self-pay, or a free cancel
pf.edges.hoursRunLow: the plan's covered hours run low: the desk is warned, and asks the doctor for more where the plan allows, or tells the client the self-pay price
pf.edges.outOfState: a video client who'll be in another state: only a dietitian licensed there, another time, or a free cancel
pf.edges.child: a child or teen: a parent or guardian books and comes; the owner OKs it
pf.edges.forms: the intake not done: one reminder, then the owner keeps the visit (filled in first), moves it, or cancels with no fee
pf.edges.weather: home visits and store tours: an ice or snow warning on the roads at 5pm the day before; Sam keeps the visit or moves it, and a move or a cancel never costs the client

notes:
From: therapist (the current overlay, itself built from physical-therapist and the dentist pilot), reviewed. Why: a dietitian's practice runs like it: visits of a set length with a named, licensed clinician; video visits counted as flow A, with the client's state asked before times and checked at the start (the old flowchart's winter-away case); the intake only on the secure page; the plan checked by hand; safety words with 988 and 911; no $2; and follow-ups agreed at the visit, then OK'd by the client's own yes. Physical-therapist has the referral but no video or crisis handling; therapist has both of those, so it fits more of this work.
Added for this work: the doctor's referral as the first step (A4-43 'The clinic must get it', A4-48, A7-33 to A7-36; B4-38, B4-42, B7-33); signs of an eating disorder as an own ending branch (A3-x01, B3-x01); the goals set by the dietitian, never Rosie (A8-44, B8-39); a plan's covered hours (A10-x02); a private rating (A10-34 'Yes' and B10-02 on); a package of follow-ups used as a credit (A5-03 on). Removed from the pilot: 'Crisis words, then still books' (self-harm gets 988 and no booking in that chat) and the yearly weekly-time reminder.
Names: Sam Lee, a registered dietitian, owns Lee Home Nutrition LLC (the master's main company: home nutrition and diabetes education, 300 Main St, a 25-mile area) and Lee Nutrition Clinic LLC (the second company: the clinic at 60 Grove St, Springfield, and video). Alex's home is 16 Cedar Ct.
People: Riley became Grace (clinic and video; families, teens and some home visits), Avery became Priya (clinic and video; licensed in a second state), Jordan became Marcus (home visits; also a certified diabetes educator), Casey became Noor (a dietitian with a provisional license, under Sam's supervision, a switch). Sam, Pat (now 'practice manager') and Alex M. stay. Alex has no pronoun.
Kinds of work: plumbing became home nutrition, electrical became diabetes education (it waits for a certified diabetes educator, where the plug-in or a plan asks), the barbershop became the nutrition clinic.
